findings.text: Aggregation helper carries pointers to hierarchical totals, hierarchy-local totals, child pending contributions, optional parent pending sink, current per-cpu values, previous per-cpu snapshot, plus an element count. It serves as a short-lived descriptor for folding per-cpu deltas upward.

Statistic folding drains pending child contributions, computes change in per-cpu values since the prior snapshot, adds per-cpu change to the local total, and adds combined change to the hierarchical total and optionally to the parent pending sink. Taken pending slots are cleared and snapshots track last observed per-cpu values.

Release of a memory group invalidates reclaim iteration state and detaches generational reclaim bookkeeping. Later freeing waits for writeback completions where configured, adjusts socket and BPF enablement references according to hierarchy mode and prior activation, then tears down pressure notification, high-limit work, legacy tree membership, shrinker metadata and the group object.

Reset restores unconstrained defaults: memory and swap ceilings at maximum, minimum and low protections at zero, memory and swap high throttle at maximum, group OOM disabled, plus writeback domain refresh and where configured zswap ceiling at maximum with writeback allowed and legacy kernel and TCP ceilings at maximum with soft limit cleared.

One build variant merges interrupt-unsafe accounting by atomically taking kernel memory and per-node reclaimable and unreclaimable slab counters and adding each taken amount to node and group totals, local totals and parent pending sinks. The alternate build variant provides an empty operation for the same hook.

Per-cpu statistics flush for a memory group first performs the interrupt-unsafe merge, then folds group-wide state counters, group-wide event counters and per-memory-node reclaim statistics for the calling processor, and finally clears per-cpu and shared update markers with the shared clear done once.

Task fork marks the object charging pointer with a lazy-update flag. Task exit removes flag bits, releases the associated reference and clears the pointer, tolerating later untracked allocations. Both transitions are described as safe without locking because they act on the current task.
Globally visible helpers in these fragments provide generational reclaim address-space membership management and migration, user-requested proactive reclaim, and formatted memory statistics display.

Generational reclaim tracks address spaces in a per-group queue. Addition resolves the owning group, records it in the address space, adjusts per-node iteration tails that were at the queue sentinel, and appends at the tail. Removal adjusts per-node iteration head and tail links referencing the departing entry, unlinks it and drops the group reference. Migration re-homes an address space when its task group differs, skipping disabled accounting, unregistered spaces and unchanged groups.

Queue membership mutation is serialized by a per-list spin lock covering tail and head adjustments and linkage changes. Peak watcher mutation and watermark updates are serialized by a per-group peaks lock. Migration expects the owning task allocation lock held and acquires task locking on the attach path before inspecting ownership and triggering migration.

Task attachment performs an optional generational reclaim step that migrates the first leader address space when the leader owns it, and a kernel memory step that atomically marks every migrating task for lazy charging refresh. One build variant makes the reclaim step empty.

Memory protection and limit tunables display the sentinel maximum as textual maximum and other values scaled to bytes. Writes trim surrounding whitespace, accept the same textual maximum, parse to pages and install into minimum, low, high or ceiling controls, with ceiling installation using an atomic exchange.

Lowering high or ceiling limits optionally attempts synchronous convergence unless nonblocking mode was requested. Each pass stops when the limit changed concurrently, usage is at or below the limit, a signal is pending or the group is dying. The first pass drains per-cpu charging stock, later passes reclaim the excess with swap allowed and bounded retries, and the ceiling path escalates to pressure event reporting and out-of-memory handling when reclaim makes no progress before yielding. Both paths refresh writeback domain sizing on exit.

Peak files distinguish never-written descriptors from active watchers via a sentinel. Opening installs the sentinel. Display shows either the global watermark or the larger of descriptor and local watermarks. Writing snapshots current usage into the local watermark, raises lagging peer watchers, registers the descriptor on first write and records its snapshot. Releasing an active descriptor unregisters it, while never-written descriptors take a fast path.
Peak descriptor sentinel denotes the never-written state and equals an all-ones unsigned long value.

Status helpers expose current usage in bytes, low high maximum out-of-memory and socket throttle event counts for hierarchical and local scopes, formatted full statistics via a temporary buffer, per-node breakdowns after forcing a statistics flush, and group out-of-memory mode as an integer. Group mode writes accept only zero or one. Manual reclaim writes delegate to proactive reclaim handling.

Proactive reclaim accepts an amount plus optional swappiness controls, requires exactly one of group or node target, trims input and rejects empty amounts or unknown options or out-of-range swappiness. Group reclaim uses group reclaim with swap and proactive mode and optional swappiness override; node reclaim uses a single-threaded node guard and a control describing priority, writeback, unmap, swap and proactive behavior with a minimum batch size.

Reclaim-like paths must cope with concurrent limit changes, pending signals with freezer restart semantics, dying groups blocked on hierarchy teardown, contended node reclaim, and bounded no-progress retries ending in failure. Progress accumulates across shrinking batches with a final attempt draining aging caches.
